## Minneapolis-area bar-service shortlist
I started with **The Knot’s Minneapolis Bar Services & Beverages directory**, which currently shows 44 results, then prioritized vendors whose profiles describe bartending, drinks, spirits, beverage supply, or full-bar service. These are solid first calls for wine/liquor service for a holiday party:

| Vendor | City/state or listed base/service area | What The Knot profile says |
|---|---|---|
| **Hercules Twin City Bartending** | Minneapolis, MN | Bar service for weddings, parties, and corporate events across greater Minnesota (and parts of Iowa/Wisconsin). |
| **Fusion Events** | Minneapolis/St. Paul/Taylors Falls, MN | Experienced bartenders; profile specifically says it handles setup/takedown and provides drinkware and beverages. |
| **Hire A Host** | Burnsville, MN | Full bar services throughout the Twin Cities; The Knot says it is licensed and insured. |
| **Blue Sky Miners** | Minneapolis, MN | Mobile bar service; profile references bartenders serving signature cocktails, **spirits**, and nonalcoholic drinks. |
| **Mix & Mingle Mobile Bar** | Saint Paul, MN (serves all Minnesota) | Dry-hire bar service with bartenders for signature cocktails, spirits, and NA drinks. “Dry hire” is a signal to confirm whether you purchase/provide the wine and liquor. |
| **With a Twist Bartending Service** | Minneapolis / serves Minnesota | Bartending service active since 2006; profile says its bartenders are TIPS-certified. |
| **Hitch & Sip** | Farmington, MN | A liquor-catering business with mobile service and equipment for an event bar. |
| **Poure Decisions** | Champlin, MN (within 100 miles listed) | Luxury mobile-bar setup and hospitality service. |

**Best quick-fit calls:** Fusion Events if you want drinks, drinkware, and setup in one package; Hire A Host if licensing/insured full-bar service is a priority; Hercules or With a Twist for established bartender-forward service; and Surdyk’s below if food plus bar coordination matters.

**Important quote checklist:** Ask each whether it (1) supplies/sells the alcohol or is bartender-only/dry-hire, (2) can source the specific wine, beer, and spirits menu, (3) includes permits/liability coverage and TIPS-certified staff, (4) supplies ice, glassware, bar, mixers, and garnish, and (5) includes setup, strike, gratuity/service charge, and travel. Those details vary materially among mobile bar providers.

**The Knot starting points**
- [Minneapolis Bar Services & Beverages directory](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/bar-services-minneapolis-mn)
- [Surdyk’s Catering & Craft Bartending profile](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/surdyks-catering-and-craft-bartending-minneapolis-mn-1026917)

## Is Surdyk’s meaningfully more full-service?
**Yes—based on the services it explicitly advertises, Surdyk’s is materially broader than the bartender/mobile-bar-focused alternatives.** It is not merely a liquor or bartender supplier.

What I found:

- **Food:** Surdyk’s describes a range from cheese boards and office drop-off lunches to a **full-scale event with a custom menu and bar service**. Its Knot profile lists buffet service, passed appetizers, chef stations, menu tastings, delivery/setup, and catering cleanup.
- **Beverage/bar:** Its own site explicitly advertises **custom menu and bar service**; its parent business also has a long-standing wine, spirits, beer, specialty-food, cheese-shop, and bar/eatery operation. That makes it particularly plausible for a coordinated food-and-drink program, though you should confirm the exact alcohol procurement/permit arrangement for your venue.
- **Event service:** The Knot profile says Surdyk’s works from menu planning through “event service” and final cleanup. Its holiday page specifically offers **full-service catering** as well as drop-off catering—well aligned with a hands-off company or home holiday party.
- **Staffing:** It plainly advertises an event-service team and final cleanup, but I did **not** see a separately itemized staffing package or stated staff-to-guest ratios in the material I read. Ask for bartender/server/chef staffing levels and hours in the proposal.
- **Rentals:** I did **not** find an explicit claim that Surdyk’s supplies rentals such as tables, chairs, linens, glassware, or a portable bar. Do not assume rentals are included; ask what it coordinates versus what you must rent separately.

So: **more full-service in food, menu planning, setup/service, and cleanup; not demonstrably more full-service in rentals from the published material.**

Sources read: [Surdyk’s Catering—About](https://www.surdykscatering.com/about), [Holiday Catering](https://www.surdykscatering.com/holiday-catering), and its [The Knot profile](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/surdyks-catering-and-craft-bartending-minneapolis-mn-1026917). Surdyk’s catering address is **2117 West River Road N., Minneapolis, MN 55411**.

## Nonalcoholic pairing: Instant Pot mulligatawny
For a warm, satisfying alcohol-free counterpart to a holiday bar menu, I’d use **Feasting at Home’s Instant Pot Mulligatawny (Curried Indian Soup)**. It is creamy, gently sweet/spiced, vegan-adaptable, and the recipe serves **4–6**. It would be especially good as a small bowl/cup service alongside bread or naan; a nonalcoholic ginger-apple spritz would echo the soup’s warming spice and apple.

### Ingredients
- 3 tablespoons ghee or coconut oil
- 1/2 teaspoon each whole cumin seeds, whole coriander seeds, and whole mustard seeds
- 1 chopped onion
- 3 roughly chopped garlic cloves
- 1 teaspoon grated ginger
- 1 serrano chile, slit lengthwise but with stem left intact (use less/omit for a mild party crowd)
- 1 tablespoon yellow curry powder
- 1 chopped carrot
- 1 cubed yam
- 1 cubed green apple
- 4 cups vegetable or chicken broth
- 1/2 cup red lentils
- 1 teaspoon sea salt
- 1 chopped tomato
- 15 ounces coconut milk
- 1/4 cup chopped parsley
- 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, leaves and stems
- 1–3 teaspoons fresh lemon juice
- Optional serving additions: yogurt, naan, basmati rice, cashews, and extra herbs.

### Straightforward method
1. Set the Instant Pot to **Sauté**. Heat the ghee/oil; toast cumin, coriander, and mustard seeds for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
2. Add onion, garlic, ginger, serrano, and curry powder. Sauté about 3 minutes, until softened.
3. Stir in carrot, yam, apple, broth, lentils, salt, tomato, and coconut milk. Scrape the pot bottom clean to prevent a burn warning.
4. Lock the lid and cook at **medium pressure for 10 minutes**.
5. Carefully vent manually once cooking is done. Stir in parsley, cilantro, and lemon; adjust salt, lemon, and heat. Serve with naan or over rice.

Recipe source: [Feasting at Home—Instant Pot Mulligatawny](https://www.feastingathome.com/instant-pot-mulligatawny/).
